images.title: Profit is income minus costs
images.purpose: Shows the lemonade stall: income ₹900 split into rent ₹200, making ₹300 and profit ₹400.
images.composition: Two bars of equal length stacked in the centre: income on top, its split below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. Top bar: one long rectangle filled teal (#0072B2) with income ₹900 written inside in white. Bottom bar of the same length directly below, split into three touching parts with widths in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 from left to right: rent ₹200 in vermilion (#D55E00), making ₹300 in a lighter vermilion tint, and profit ₹400 in green (#009E73), each label in white inside its part. Above the top bar, centred, small: 60 × ₹15 in dark text. Exactly 2 bars, the lower one in 3 parts; no stall, no glasses, no people.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Profit is what is left of the income after all the costs.
images.description: Shows the lemonade stall: income ₹900 split into rent ₹200, making ₹300 and profit ₹400.

image_decisions.why: A bar model shows profit as the part of income left after costs, the step students most often get wrong.
